svg.text: Centre of Mass under Three Layout Scenarios
Neutral posture · side-view estimate · head-borne and body-borne mass reported separately
Reference architecture · built-in battery retained as rear mass
Rear power offsets the front optics,
but the whole system mass remains on the head.
Current proposal · battery removed from the head
Head-borne mass falls, while the estimated
centre of mass becomes more anterior.
Sensitivity scenario · compute and support shifted posterior
A small posterior redistribution reduces the
lever arm without returning the battery to the head.
Known: published total masses and system architecture.
Estimated: module mass ranges, COM envelope and M*.
Dimensionless comparison; not a measured neck torque.
External power reduces head-borne mass but also
is required to reduce both mass and static moment.
Indicative design estimate, not a measured ergonomic result. Module-level masses are not publicly disclosed; values are shown as ranges. Body-worn power is excluded from head-borne COM.
Reference anchors: Microsoft HoloLens 2 hardware; Magic Leap 2 Operations Manual; Apple Vision Pro Tech Specs; Chihara & Seo (2018); Astrologo et al. (2024).
